target.title: refactor(infra): consolidate home path helpers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Wave 3 of the shared utility consolidation found that canonical OpenClaw home-path behavior was split between `src/infra/home-dir.ts` and generic `src/utils.ts`. Resolution already had a focused owner, while `resolveUserPath` was duplicated and user-facing home presentation remained embedded in the broad utility module.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Makes `src/infra/home-dir.ts` the single owner for effective/OS home resolution and user-path expansion.
- Moves display-only home shortening into focused internal `src/infra/home-dir-display.ts`.
- Keeps `src/utils.ts` as the existing compatibility facade, preserving export identity and callers.
- Keeps terminal token-safe display, daemon/service policy, sandbox containment, config/state ownership, URL/media paths, shell expansion, and package/plugin-local contracts separate.
- Avoids expanding `openclaw/plugin-sdk/infra-runtime`; the display module is not part of an SDK barrel.

## User Impact

No intended behavior change. HOME/USERPROFILE/homedir precedence, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `~`/`~/`/`~\\`, unsupported `~user`, blank/relative/absolute paths, separators, normalization, fallback behavior, and display prefixes remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/home-dir.test.ts src/infra/home-dir-display.test.ts src/utils.test.ts` — 3 shards, 41 tests passed on the rebased head.
- Testbox-through-Crabbox `tbx_01kwn62ve4kgj861grf9rrdcsn` / Actions run 28688257004 — `pnpm check:changed`, full `pnpm build`, plugin SDK export validation, and `pnpm check:import-cycles` passed; zero runtime value cycles.
- Final autoreview: `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` — clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Live GitHub overlap search found no existing home-path/home-dir/tilde consolidation PR or issue.
- Production LOC is neutral, while six duplicate ownership concepts are removed from `src/utils.ts`; total diff is 134 additions / 155 deletions.
